name: Libertarianism
summary: Libertarianism treats individual liberty as the highest political value and holds that force may be used only to defend people's rights, not to make them serve others or themselves. Built on self-ownership and strong property rights, it wants a sharply limited government, free markets, free trade and free movement, low or no taxes and no redistribution. It also defends civil liberties: free speech, gun rights, legal drugs and sex work, privacy from surveillance, and non-interventionist foreign policy.
scope: Mainstream contemporary right-libertarianism, chiefly in its US form: the Libertarian Party platform, Nozick's minimal-state theory, and Cato-style libertarianism as set out by David Boaz, with Hayek and Friedman as consequentialist influences. Where the family splits (minarchism versus anarcho-capitalism, abortion), the answers follow the mainstream or record the split. It excludes left-libertarianism, libertarian socialism and Objectivism, and treats anarcho-capitalism and paleolibertarianism as strands rather than the centre.

keyFigures.name: Friedrich Hayek
keyFigures.role: Economist and influence on libertarianism, defender of limited government and free markets

sources.title: Libertarianism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Non-aggression principle, right-libertarianism as the dominant US form, non-interventionism, opposition to spending on health and welfare, drug legalization, currency competition

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Libertarian Party wants a free market in medical care without government licensing or mandates, and libertarians oppose tax-funded spending on health as coercive redistribution.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Libertarians reject government price controls, which the party platform says include wages, and economists in the tradition such as Friedman argue minimum wages price low-skilled workers out of jobs.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Voluntary exchange and dispersed knowledge (Hayek) are the core economic case of the movement; planners cannot know what markets coordinate.

public-ownership.rationale: The platform says government should not compete with private enterprise; state ownership of industry is the opposite of the libertarian program.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Redistributive taxation is likened by Nozick to forced labor, and the party opposes any tax increase and seeks the eventual end of taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Libertarians defend the freedom to form or refuse a union but oppose compulsory dues and legal privileges for unions, and generally doubt that unions benefit workers or society as a whole; the overall judgment is inferred from that stance.

property-fundamental.rationale: Robust property rights grounded in self-ownership and just acquisition are central, and the party opposes eminent domain and civil asset forfeiture.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Libertarians call for deregulation and oppose licensing and government control of business; they also oppose corporate privileges, but by separating business and state rather than by more regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The party would phase out Social Security and leave aid to private charity, and libertarian writers such as Charles Murray argue benefits discourage people from taking responsibility for themselves.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker cooperatives are acceptable if chosen voluntarily, but right-libertarians reject any norm or policy that workers should own their firms in place of private owners.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The platform commits to ending government spying on everyone and extending Fourth Amendment protection to records held by third parties.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug use is the standard victimless crime that libertarians would repeal laws against, arguing prohibition creates black markets and violence.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Libertarians support full freedom of expression; the platform says offensive language is not grounds for legal action.

strong-leader.rationale: Libertarianism is built on constitutionally limited government and against what the party calls the cult of the omnipotent state; a leader freed of checks is the danger it guards against.

state-harmful.rationale: The family is split between minarchists who want a night-watchman state and anarcho-capitalists who want none; the mainstream (Nozick, Cato, the party's support for a defensive military) still holds that a minimal state for police, courts and defense is legitimate.

limit-guns.rationale: The platform opposes laws restricting, registering or monitoring firearms and ammunition.

empower-police-military.rationale: Libertarians oppose militarism and world policing and want to abolish qualified immunity; they want a smaller military and more accountable police, not more power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The party supports the right of consenting adults to buy and sell sexual services, and prostitution bans are listed among laws libertarians oppose.

decide-locally.rationale: Libertarians favor decentralization and recognize self-determination down to secession, though their deeper preference is for individuals, not any level of government, to decide.

rehabilitation.rationale: The platform emphasizes restitution to victims and opposes overcharging and the death penalty; this anti-punitive leaning is the basis for a mild agreement, inferred rather than stated.

traditional-family.rationale: The doctrine holds government should not define or promote any kind of relationship; individual libertarians range from socially conservative right-libertarians to culturally liberal ones, so as a political claim it is neutral.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Libertarians would take government out of licensing marriage, but until then the platform says licenses should go to all consenting adults, and Boaz counts rights for gay people as progress.

abortion-legal.rationale: Libertarians are genuinely split: self-ownership arguments support choice while the right-to-life principle against initiated force supports protecting the fetus, and the party platform now takes no position.

more-religion-public.rationale: The party opposes government action that aids or attacks any religion; religion is a private, voluntary matter, though libertarians have no objection to it flourishing in civil society.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Libertarians want government to be strictly race-neutral, letting private parties respond to discrimination through boycotts, and oppose state programs to remedy group injustices.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Libertarianism is a narrow theory of government's role, not a comprehensive doctrine, and takes no stance on this question; adherents differ.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Libertarian individualism and cosmopolitan support for trade and migration put little weight on national culture, which should evolve through free choice; inferred from these principles.

gradual-change.rationale: Hayekian libertarians value evolved institutions and incremental reform, while the party program seeks to abolish taxation and much of the state; the family is split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The platform holds that economic freedom demands unrestricted movement of people across borders, and the scholarship places libertarians with the left in opposing border restrictions; a paleolibertarian minority dissents.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Libertarians favor peace with all nations and entangling alliances with none, and oppose concentrating power above national governments; inferred from the platform's foreign policy.

free-trade.rationale: The party supports removing all governmental impediments to trade, and Boaz credits open markets with spreading prosperity.

nation-first.rationale: Libertarians reject both nationalism and supranational governance: they favor non-intervention and no alliances, but also free trade and migration with all; the statement's framing does not fit them.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Non-interventionism is a defining libertarian commitment; the platform opposes military aid, sanctions and regime change.

open-borders.rationale: The platform calls for unrestricted movement of people across borders, and libertarians are described as opposing border restrictions; a restrictionist minority dissents.

limit-growth.rationale: Libertarians favor economic growth through free markets and would handle environmental harm through property rights and restitution, not growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The platform rejects government control of energy prices and production and treats environmental protection as a matter of enforcing property rights, ruling out sweeping state climate programs.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Libertarians are optimistic about progress through trade and innovation in free markets; this is inferred from that optimism rather than stated.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The party opposes subsidizing any form of energy, so libertarians would expand nuclear power only by removing regulatory barriers and letting markets decide; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: The platform affirms the people's right to alter, abolish or withdraw from a government that destroys liberty, while the non-aggression principle limits force to defense.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hayek's argument that knowledge is dispersed and that central planners cannot match individuals acting on their own knowledge cuts against rule by experts, though libertarians do not exalt majorities either.

central-planning.rationale: Opposition to central planning, grounded in Hayek's and Mises's knowledge and calculation arguments, is foundational.

socialized-markets.rationale: Right-libertarians defend private ownership of the means of production and voluntary capitalist exchange, not markets restricted to worker or public ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Left-libertarians and geolibertarians favor land taxes, but mainstream right-libertarians accept private appropriation of land without equality constraints and oppose taxes generally.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Bequests are voluntary transfers of justly held property, and the party opposes all forcible collection of money from individuals.

basic-income.rationale: Most libertarians oppose state redistribution; some (left-libertarians, and Friedman's negative income tax as a welfare replacement) support versions of it, so the mainstream disagrees without strong force.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The platform opposes tariffs and all governmental barriers to trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy is central planning in miniature and contradicts the principle that government should not direct or compete with private enterprise.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Right-libertarians judge holdings by how they were acquired, not by their pattern, so they reject engineering a wider spread of property, though they oppose state ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Voluntary exchange, including wage labor and money, is for libertarians the ideal basis of human relations.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The platform calls for free-market banking and an end to inflationary policy and legal tender laws, and Javier Milei campaigned on currency competition; Friedman-style monetarists would keep a rule-bound central bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-set wages and prices are the price controls the platform opposes, and libertarians oppose compulsory arbitration.

one-party-rule.rationale: Libertarians champion pluralism, open political systems and limited government, against any party monopoly on power.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule sits poorly with equal individual rights and constitutionally limited government, though a minority (Hoppe) prefers monarchy to democracy; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Libertarians welcome open and democratic systems but rank constitutional limits on majority power above democracy, and public choice theory makes them skeptical of what voters produce.

direct-votes.rationale: Libertarians care more about limiting what any majority may decide than about how it decides; some back ballot initiatives for reforms such as cannabis legalization, but there is no doctrine either way.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power is a socialist institution at odds with private property and constitutionally limited government; inferred from rejection of socialism.

right-to-secede.rationale: The platform recognizes the right to political self-determination including secession, which it says needs no one else's permission.

natural-rulers.rationale: All individuals are sovereign over their own lives and hold equal rights; no one has a natural title to rule others.

political-violence-never.rationale: Libertarians forbid initiating force but permit defensive force, and the platform affirms the right to abolish a destructive government, so violence is not ruled out in every case.

war-builds-character.rationale: Libertarians oppose war and militarism and favor toleration and trade over war; war expands the state.

separate-church-state.rationale: The platform opposes any government action that aids or attacks any religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Laws should be limited to violations of others' rights by force or fraud, and libertarianism is a political theory shared by theists and atheists alike.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists hold that all protective services could be private, and many minarchists accept private arbitration and security even while keeping a state military; the statement says only that it could be done.

military-superiority.rationale: The platform wants a military sufficient to defend against aggression, not one to police the world.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Libertarian individualism treats people as individuals, not members of ethnic groups, and the platform rejects denying rights based on ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Libertarians see voluntary exchange as mutually beneficial rather than as class exploitation; only the left-libertarian fringe sees the state as a tool of a ruling class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Justice is historical: holdings acquired by just means are just whatever pattern results, so pursuing equal outcomes requires illegitimate redistribution.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The platform's principle of rectification of past injustice in property supports returning wrongly seized land to its owners; applying it to indigenous peoples is inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Rectification is owed by and to particular wrongdoers and victims, so libertarians reject taxpayer-funded reparations between states; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Libertarians oppose building larger political units around religion or civilization and favor no entangling alliances.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Libertarians regard peaceful pursuit of one's own ends as legitimate and socially beneficial through exchange; egoists such as Rand go further, while others are neutral on its morality.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individuals are normatively primary and enforceable duties are limited to not violating others' rights; there are no enforceable positive duties to the community.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Libertarians protect the environment through property rights and restitution for harm to people, a human-centered approach; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Population control would override self-ownership in the most personal decisions; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Libertarians credit markets and industrial trade with the spread of prosperity and liberty.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Libertarians welcome innovation and oppose regulation that protects incumbents, though they don't call for the state to speed it up; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Self-ownership means people may do as they choose with their own bodies, ruling out paternalist bans.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Libertarians want government decision-making shrunk, not automated, and doubt any central planner, human or machine; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The platform opposes government spying and demands privacy for personal records; strong private encryption follows.

restore-past-order.rationale: Mainstream libertarians such as Boaz tell a story of expanding liberty and toleration, though a reactionary right-libertarian strand looks backward; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Natural-rights libertarians judge institutions by principle while consequentialist libertarians such as Friedman judge them by results; the family is split.

direct-action.rationale: Mainstream libertarians work through the Libertarian Party, elections and policy advocacy; agorists who reject electoral politics are a minority strand.

means-match-ends.rationale: Because libertarians reject initiating force, they hold that liberty must be pursued by peaceful, voluntary means; inferred from the non-aggression principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Libertarians credit markets, property and the division of labour with modern prosperity and see the extended market order as civilization's achievement.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hayek and the market tradition treat specialisation coordinated by prices as how dispersed knowledge is used and wealth created.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Nozick's entitlement theory rejects patterned principles like distribution by need: holdings are just if acquired and transferred justly.

production-for-use.rationale: Libertarians hold that free markets and the profit motive are the best way to meet people's needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Libertarians see profit as the outcome of voluntary exchange and entrepreneurship, and Nozick rejects the claim that market wage labour is exploitative.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Libertarians reject any concentration of coercive power, let alone a class dictatorship that abolishes property.

collective-farming.rationale: Libertarians defend private property in land and individual enterprise; voluntary communes are permitted but collectivisation is the opposite of their ideal.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Libertarians argue that free trade promotes peace and that war is driven by the state, which grows through it.

taxation-theft.rationale: Nozick likens redistributive taxation to forced labor and the party opposes all forcible collection of money from individuals.

harm-principle.rationale: Libertarians hold that law should reach only violations of others' rights by force or fraud and want victimless crimes repealed.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Libertarianism is built on the rights of individuals, and its advocates treat claims of group rights as collectivism; Boaz describes individuals as the bearers of rights.

conscription.rationale: Opposition to conscription is a standard libertarian commitment, named by both Boaz and the party platform.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Libertarians are sceptical that voting restrains government and stress free movement and the right of secession; inferred from the platform, which backs secession, and the free-migration position.

state-as-business.rationale: Libertarians want a minimal state limited to protecting rights, or competing private providers, not a state run by an owner-manager; neocameralism grew out of but broke with libertarianism.

media-academia-power.rationale: Libertarians locate the danger in state power and government expansion, not in universities and the press; inferred, as mainstream libertarianism does not advance this claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Mainstream libertarians treat people as individuals and reject racial collectivism, though paleolibertarian figures have flirted with hereditarian claims; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation by trades and communities is the opposite of libertarian individualism, though libertarians are also sceptical of party politics.

total-state.rationale: Libertarians want the state confined to protecting individual rights, with culture, education and the economy left to voluntary action.

national-rebirth.rationale: Libertarians are wary of nationalism as collectivist and state-expanding; inferred from their rejection of nationalism and militarism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The party platform and mainstream libertarians favour non-intervention and oppose imperialism and wars of conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Libertarians want rule by impartial law protecting equal individual rights, not personal hierarchies of lords and vassals; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Self-ownership, the foundation of libertarianism, rules out being legally bound to land or forced to labour for another.

knowledge-power.rationale: Libertarians, following Hayek, stress the limits of central knowledge but not that knowledge is a product of power; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: The natural-rights strand holds that rights are universal and knowable by reason, while the consequentialist strand of Hayek and Friedman makes no such claim.

single-common-good.rationale: Libertarians reject a single social goal imposed on all; individuals pursue their own ends and the state only protects the framework of rights.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Libertarians have no shared position on Israel: non-interventionists oppose US support for any foreign state, while others back Israel as a liberal democracy; inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Libertarians would let anyone migrate, diaspora members included, but reject citizenship defined by ancestry or nationhood, so the statement's premise does not fit; inferred from the open-migration position.

revive-national-language.rationale: Libertarians oppose the state imposing a language or funding cultural programs, leaving language to individual choice; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The platform leaves firms to private owners and their employees, favouring voluntary bargaining without government mandates, so imposed worker or public votes on management conflict with property rights; the platform does not address board seats directly.

school-vouchers.rationale: The platform says education is best provided by the free market and that parents should control all funds spent on their children's education, which supports school choice; many libertarians see vouchers only as a step short of ending public funding, and the platform does not name them.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The platform states that government should not incur debt, which burdens future generations without their consent, and Keynesian stimulus is contrary to the free-market view.

economic-freedom.rationale: Libertarians hold that property rights and free exchange are the foundation of all other liberties, and the party and Boaz argue that state economic control leads to control of everything else.

rule-by-example.rationale: Libertarians distrust the virtue of those in power and want rights secured by clear, limited law and the courts; the platform and Boaz stress constitutional limits on rulers rather than trust in their example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred from the platform's support for secession and self-government, which libertarians ground in individual consent and association rather than in nationhood.

force-without-un.rationale: Libertarians hold force is justified only in defense of rights and oppose military adventures abroad, so they reject unilateral intervention, though they would act without UN approval to defend the country itself; inferred from the platform's non-interventionism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Libertarians favor reason and evidence, but the family includes religious and traditionalist currents alongside secular rationalists, and the platform only defends freedom of belief; adherents are split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Libertarians mainly want to abolish welfare for everyone and oppose border limits, so they reject citizen-only benefits in principle; some accept restricting benefits as a second-best to keep borders open.

missingStatements.text: The government should be able to conscript citizens into military service.
missingStatements.rationale: Opposition to conscription is a standard libertarian commitment, named by both Boaz and the party platform as something government must not do.

missingStatements.text: Acts between consenting adults that harm no one else should never be crimes.
missingStatements.rationale: The principle that law should reach only violations of others' rights by force or fraud, and the repeal of victimless crimes, defines libertarian criminal justice beyond any single issue.

missingStatements.text: Taxation is a form of theft or forced labor.
missingStatements.rationale: Nozick likens redistributive taxation to forced labor and the party opposes all forcible collection of money from individuals, a claim distinct from how high taxes should be.

notes: The family is split between minarchists and anarcho-capitalists (separate catalog entries), and on abortion and, since the 2022 rise of the Mises Caucus, on immigration. Left-libertarians would answer differently on land-value tax, basic income and class. The answers follow mainstream US right-libertarianism.
